articles.title_orig: Jim Copenhaver, man shot in Trump assassination attempt, dies 2 years later
articles.title_zh: Jim Copenhaver, man shot in Trump assassination attempt, dies 2 years later
articles.content_orig:
A man who was injured two years ago in an assassination attempt on Donald Trump has died, his family said in a statement Thursday. He was 76.
Jim Copenhaver sustained what his family described as “life-altering” injuries after being shot in Butler, Pennsylvania, on July 13, 2024. He was attending a campaign rally held by Trump when a gunman named Thomas Crooks opened fire.
He died Wednesday “surrounded by his loved ones,” according to a statement from Joseph A. Feldman, an attorney representing Copenhaver’s family. The statement did not provide a cause of death.
Serving his country was a “defining” aspect of Copenhaver’s life, his family said, and he was deeply grateful for the outpouring of love he received following the Butler shooting.
“As a veteran, he proudly served our nation in the armed forces, and his love of country never wavered,” the statement said. “James was a true American patriot who believed deeply in the freedoms and ideals upon which this nation was founded, and he embodied the very best traits of our great nation.”
The family released a statement through a spokesperson for Allegheny Health Network at the time Copenhaver was discharged. They thanked the public for their support as the family dealt with the aftermath of the “horrible, senseless, and unnecessary act of violence.”
Copenhaver was hit once in the triceps and again in his abdomen, leaving him with nerve damage and requiring doctors to transect some of his colon.
Months later, he told NBC News he lost 30 pounds and had to walk with a cane. He hadn’t even realized he was shot until he saw part of his sleeve “go away.”
“I mean, I heard it distinctly,” Copenhaver said of the shooting. “I turn around to my friend and I said, ‘I think I was shot.’ And that’s when I got the second one.”
Former fire chief Corey Comperatore died in the shooting, and Copenhaver was one of two people injured in the attack. Trump’s ear was hit by either a bullet or a fragment but was not seriously injured, the FBI said.
Crooks, 20, was shot and killed by a Secret Service sharpshooter. A motive was never uncovered in the shooting even after law enforcement officials interviewed Crooks’ relatives, neighbors, teachers and classmates .
The official X account for the House Republicans posted about Copenhaver’s death, expressing the GOP’s condolences to his family.
“Jim endured unimaginable hardship with strength and perseverance,” the post said. “We join his family and loved ones in mourning his loss and praying for them during this difficult time. May he rest in peace.”

articles.title_orig: Israel’s Netanyahu takes the U.N. stage facing global isolation and a fight for his political future
articles.title_zh: Israel’s Netanyahu takes the U.N. stage facing global isolation and a fight for his political future
articles.content_orig:
Delegates walk out of Netanyahu’s UN speech
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has used his platform at the United Nations General Assembly to attack detractors and allies alike, and his presence sparked uproar in the chamber.
Speaking before the UNGA on Thursday, Netanyahu attacked New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, critics and Iran’s leadership, as well as allied countries like the United Kingdom and France.
Back home, the prime minister is locked in a tight race to stay in power ahead of an election on October 27, and analysts say his UNGA speech was aimed as much at people back home as it was at international viewers.
Dozens of envoys from around the world walked out as the speech began, some jeering and booing, while Netanyahu’s own team stood and applauded, and the speaker of the session shouted for order.
“If there are any other moral cowards who haven’t left this hall, please do so now,” Netanyahu said to those turning their backs on him.
He addressed the war that the US and Israel launched on Iran in February, saying: “Devastating Iran’s nuclear facilities was hard, was very hard to do.”
“But for me, it was one of the easiest decisions I’ve ever had to make as prime minister”, claiming that if he had not, “we’d all be dead”, he added.
In his own speech before the UNGA on Wednesday, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also addressed the nuclear issue and called out the “double standard”.
“The nuclear weapon is in Israel, but the inspectors are in Iran. Israel kills, but Iran is subject to sanctions,” Pezeshkian said.
Netanyahu on Thursday said that Israel was fighting a “seven-front war”, including Gaza, the occupied West Bank, Syria, Lebanon, Iran, Yemen’s Houthis and militias in Iraq.
“We are going to win. We have no other choice,” Netanyahu declared, repeating the words of his older brother Yonatan Netanyahu, who was killed in 1976 during Operation Entebbe in Uganda.
The United Kingdom and France, historic partners of Israel, were also in Netanyahu’s firing line. They have become increasingly outspoken in their criticism of the country’s actions and have both imposed limited sanctions on Israeli exports from the occupied West Bank.
“They accuse Israel, tiny Israel, of colonialism – some colonialism. And who’s accusing us? Among them are people in Britain and in France. For God’s sakes, they invented the term,” he said.
But Netanyahu thanked his “friend”, United States President Donald Trump.
“In this battle against the barbarians, we’ve had no greater partner than President Trump,” he said, as the US delegation joined the Israeli one in applauding Netanyahu’s remark.
“I thank him,” said Netanyahu, adding that Israel and the US had acted together as pilots from both countries “flew joint missions over the skies of Iran”.
Netanyahu said the US and Israel also “worked together to bring back our remaining hostages [from Gaza]”, as he defended Israeli actions in the enclave against charges of genocide.
“To all those spreading lies about my country, whether they sit in this hall or in the office of the anti-Semitic mayor of New York, I say this: shame on you,” Netanyahu said as he attacked Zohran Mamdani, who had previously said he would push for the arrest of the Israeli prime minister during his visit to the city.
“Mr Mamdani, you tried to stop me from coming here. You tried to silence me. Well, you can’t silence me,” Netanyahu said as he denied that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza.
Reacting to Netanyahu’s comments, Mamdani called the accusations against him “baseless lies” meant to “sanitise his genocide of Palestinians”.
Since October 7, 2023, Israel has faced repeated accusations of genocide in Gaza, as well as systematic war crimes in Gaza and the occupied West Bank.
The Hague-based International Criminal Court (ICC) said in 2024 it had reasonable grounds to believe Netanyahu was responsible for war crimes in Gaza, where over 73,000 Palestinians have been killed. Netanyahu denies the ICC charges.
Netanyahu attended the UNGA meeting despite an ICC warrant calling for his arrest. While he was welcomed, the Trump administration denied a visa for Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas, who addressed the UNGA through a prerecorded video statement from Ramallah earlier in the day.
As Netanyahu spoke, activists from US-based organisation Jewish Voice for Peace protested outside, accusing the United Nations of “playing host to a war criminal”.
“All across New York, Jews, Palestinians and people of conscience are rising up to demand an end to US support for the livestreamed horrors, rigged ceasefires and forever wars,” Sonya Meyerson-Knox, the group’s communications director, told Al Jazeera.
Meyerson-Knox said that “solidarity with Palestinian freedom has never been greater, and here in the US we are demanding with one voice to stop arming Israel”.
Adding to tensions, dozens of protesters, some brandishing “stop the genocide” banners, gathered near the UN. Several demonstrators were detained, including prominent actor Susan Sarandon.
Inside the UN, but addressing divisions back home in Israel, Netanyahu said: “Throughout this long war, our goal never wavers – to win with unwavering resolve … What unites us is so much stronger: our history, our values, our courage.”
Ariel Cohen, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council’s Eurasia Center, said the Israeli prime minister delivered a “good speech” at the UNGA but that he did so in the “wrong forum”.
“That speech should be given at an election rally in Israel; this is who he’s communicating to,” Cohen told Al Jazeera. “He is making points that should be made to the Israeli audience for his political survival.”
Netanyahu is only making a whirlwind stop in New York before rushing back to Israel, where the election campaign is in full swing. He is not scheduled to meet any top US leaders.

articles.title_orig: Caleb Flynn’s former mistress took the stand at his murder trial. Here’s what we learned
articles.title_zh: Caleb Flynn’s former mistress took the stand at his murder trial. Here’s what we learned
articles.content_orig:
As Caleb Flynn’s former lover Alleigha Botner sat on the stand, a prosecutor opened a cardboard box and presented her with a hefty red book to read aloud.
Then he gave her another. And then another.
34 books later, the jury had heard key firsthand evidence about their illicit affair, Flynn’s hatred for his wife, Ashley, and his desire to kill her.
“I was up until 4 a.m. last night crying, literally thinking of ways to kill her and not go to jail,” Flynn wrote in a message to Botner on August 22, 2025.
Those 34 books, organized into three cardboard boxes in court, constituted a transcript of the 107,000 messages Flynn and Botner exchanged during a 1.5-year love affair from 2024 to around early 2026. Botner testified over two days about their relationship, reading snippets from the books that showed in intimate detail affection, jealousy, hatred and violent fantasizing.
Prosecutors say the books show the motive for why Caleb Flynn, a former “American Idol” contestant and church worship leader, murdered his wife in February and staged the crime scene to make it look like she was killed by an intruder.
An affair, a missing gun and 100,000 messages: What we learned on Day 1 of testimony in Caleb Flynn’s trial
Flynn, 40, has pleaded not guilty. His defense has acknowledged he sent the messages and cheated on his wife, but said the prosecution lacks key evidence, such as the murder weapon, to prove he committed a crime.
In an interview Thursday, Botner’s attorney said it was difficult for the 24-year-old to take the stand because it “brought up a time in her life that she’s not proud of.”
“She was younger, she was a lot more naïve, and she said a lot of things that obviously no one would ever expect would be publicized to the world,” Nicholas Gounaris told CNN. “She’s not proud of what she said and she’s not proud of how she acted.”
Though the prospect of testifying was daunting, Botner felt she could provide information that would help prosecutors advance their case, Gounaris said.
“Right now, she’s very relieved that her part in this trial is over with,” he said.
Here are the key takeaways from Botner’s testimony.
Botner was 21 years old when she met Flynn at their Ohio church in 2022. She was an intern at the time, and he was a volunteer on the worship team, she said. They struck up a romantic relationship in March 2024 and it continued until the following winter, she testified.
Their romance was passionate but messy. They saw each other at least once a week and traveled to nearby cities where no one would recognize them, and they discussed getting married one day, she said. At the same time, she suspected Flynn hacked into her phone and Instagram account during their relationship, although he denied it, Botner testified.
They got matching Harry Potter lightning bolt tattoos , she said. Hers was on her forearm, but his was in his armpit because “he didn’t want Ashley to see,” she testified.
The two exchanged over 100,000 texts during their relationship – about 300 a day – between iMessage, WhatsApp and GroupMe for privacy from others.
In August 2025, Ashley Flynn found out about the affair by seeing their texts during a cruise for their 15-year wedding anniversary. Ashley reached out to Botner for a meeting, but Botner said she was too busy, she testified.
The relationship began to break down after that. Botner repeatedly asked Flynn to leave his wife, but he declined to do so, citing his two daughters, his job working with his in-laws and his reputation. After she set a final deadline in January, she told him to stop contacting her.
“It’s time for me to put my big girl pants on, be strong and officially move on from you and us,” she texted him on January 11.
In scores of texts to Botner, Flynn said that he hated his wife and referred to her by the crude codename “ douche .” Early in their relationship, he said he wished she was dead.
“I just want her dead and gone,” he wrote in early 2025.
He even asked Botner to help.
“What can I do?” Botner wrote on March 24, 2025.
“Kill her,” Flynn responded, referring to his wife.
Later, Flynn even fantasized about killing her himself.
“If I could literally kill her and not go to hell, I would do it in a heartbeat. That’s how dark and hateful I feel,” he wrote on May 16, 2025.
In one instance, Botner spoke similarly. “I want to kill her, Caleb,” she wrote in a July 2025 text. “That makes two of us,” Flynn responded.
Botner cried in court as she read that text aloud, saying she regretted writing it and “didn’t mean it.”
And in another text from August 2025, she said she just wanted him to divorce her, not kill her.
“I’m not asking that you take her life, obviously, because that’s not what you should do, and I know you actually wouldn’t,” Botner wrote to him. “But to make the divorce happen, it would change everything.”
In a spree of texts to Botner on February 15, Flynn said he was going to tell his wife he planned to leave her and get a divorce the following day.
“It’s kind of crazy. I’m not scared tomorrow. I mean, I’m not looking forward to it, and it’s about to be a crap-fest here moving forward, but I’m not scared of it,” Flynn wrote.
Botner said she was house-sitting at a pastor’s home that night. On the morning of the 16th, she received a message from a church congregant asking if she had heard “about Mrs. Flynn,” and she was sent an article about her death.
“My heart started pounding,” Botner said. “It seemed like too much of a coincidence that the day he’s divorcing her, she’s just dead all of a sudden.”
Hours after Ashley’s death, Flynn and Botner met at his in-laws’ house, where members of their church were gathered. When Botner arrived, Flynn hugged her, she testified.
“It didn’t happen the way we thought it would, did it?” Flynn said, according to her testimony.
Botner asked Flynn a lot of questions about how the shooting happened, she testified, telling the court she was “very suspicious.”
Flynn told her he had been sleeping on the couch when he heard a gunshot, saw the garage side door open and found Ashley dead in the bedroom.
“He said he saw blood everywhere. He told me he’ll never forget that sight,” Botner testified.
The testimony contradicted Flynn’s statement to investigators that he was lying down in his daughters’ bedroom when the shooting occurred.
Botner admitted to trying to hide evidence of her affair by deleting messages and lying to the FBI.
After first hearing of Ashley’s death, she said she messaged Flynn and asked him what was going on, whether he was involved and if it was real. He did not respond, and she later deleted the messages, she testified.
“Since there was a murder involved, I knew that they would probably be searching his phone, and if they saw any messages between us anywhere, the affair would be found out,” she said.
In addition, she said she lied to the FBI in her first interview on February 20.
“I was selfishly afraid that my reputation was going to be ruined and that I was going to lose my job,” she testified. “And now that there was a murder attached, I didn’t want to be attached to that in any way.”
She hired an attorney and came clean to the FBI on February 26, she testified.
The defense questioned Botner for about an hour during cross-examination.
For one, Botner said she was not entirely convinced Flynn truly hated his wife.
“I would see text messages on his phone from her saying that she loves him,” she said. Ashley’s seemingly loving nature toward Flynn made Botner think “he was also loving towards her.”
Botner allowed that Flynn “might have been” saying he hated Ashley to make her feel better due to her own insecurity.
In addition, she said, she did not believe Flynn meant it when he said he wanted to kill his wife.
“I didn’t think he could ever be capable of doing something like that,” she said.
Yet in her direct testimony Wednesday, she said she now believed he did it.
“I hate him,” Botner said. “Because I believe that he murdered his wife.”
CNN’s Isa Mudann

articles.title_orig: Trump administration launches pro-Trump TV ad ahead of midterms
articles.title_zh: Trump administration launches pro-Trump TV ad ahead of midterms
articles.content_orig:
A new ad campaign glorifying President Trump is on the air on national cable and national networks including CBS beginning Thursday, and it's being paid for by American taxpayers.
The first ad, which hit the airwaves Wednesday and aired on Fox News Channel, opens with Mr. Trump vowing, "We will defeat communism, socialism and Marxism in America." Set over a soundtrack of JMSN's song "Love Me," flash-cut random shots from the president's second administration appear with text on screen. The photos show the president at rallies, pardoning turkeys, at the White House with Christmas decorations, standing with the FIFA trophy, surrounded by flags, flanked by military leaders, outside the Taj Mahal, and more.
The ad repeatedly flashes "America will never be a communist country" on screen and also touts his administration's tax cuts and other broad expressions of support for domestic manufacturing and law enforcement in text on screen. It ends with the voice of Dana White, CEO of the Ultimate Fighting Championship, declaring, "He's the toughest, most resilient (man) I've ever met and nothing was going to stop him from fighting so hard for the country he loves."
In a post on X , JMSN said he did not grant a license for the use of "Love Me."
"To anybody who has followed my career and knows what I stand for and built my career on, it should go without saying that I would never authorize my music to be used for ANY political agenda or campaign," he said, and he indicated that no one asked him for permission to use it.
The ad, which appeared Wednesday night during "Primetime with Jesse Watters" and on Thursday afternoon, contains an on-screen disclosure that it was "Paid for by the U.S. Government."
A second ad that recounts the U.S. capture of former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife and features Mr. Trump and his top Cabinet officials aired on CBS stations and other networks Thursday evening. CBS News has learned that there are multiple versions of the ads, with some 30 seconds long and others 60 seconds. The U.S. government produced the content and paid for the air time through an ad agency.
The White House, in response to CBS News' inquiries about the pro-Trump ad, denied it was a political ad and called it a "public service announcement."
"These public service announcements are about reminding Americans to love their country and understand what makes it worth defending, at home, at our borders, and abroad," a White House spokesperson said. "The ad is educational and unapologetically patriotic. We should be proud of our country."
A White House official said the PSAs "are clearly not political," and noted, "The President is not on the ballot and the ads don't have a call to action."
Previous presidents have run PSAs, too. During the Biden administration, all of the living presidents except Mr. Trump appeared in a PSA to encourage Americans to obtain a COVID vaccination.
Democratic Sen. Maggie Hassan of New Hampshire wrote to White House chief of staff Susie Wiles to demand information about the cost of running the ad and said it "raises deep concerns about the Trump Administration's use of taxpayer dollars."
"The advertisement does not have a clear official government purpose and appears to run afoul of federal prohibitions against the use of appropriated funds as part of 'a general propaganda effort designed to aid a political party or candidates,'" Hassan wrote. She also asked the White House for information about the contractors involved, the source of the funding and whether funding was diverted from federal agencies in order to run the ad.
In another letter to Wiles, the top Democratic appropriators in the House and Senate demanded that the ad be immediately pulled from air, saying it was a violation of federal law.
"This is the sort of government propaganda one might expect in North Korea, not the United States of America, and it is an egregious and illegal misuse of Americans' hard-earned tax dollars," Sen. Patty Murray of Washington, Sen. Jack Reed of Rhode Island, Rep. Rosa DeLauro of Connecticut and Rep. Steny Hoyer of Maryland wrote.
Campaign finance experts said the commercial likely does not violate election law, even as it generated scrutiny on social media for appearing to be a campaign ad.
"It doesn't appear to be supporting or endorsing a candidate for public office," said Richard Briffault, a law professor at Columbia University. Briffault, however, agreed with Hassan that there are questions about whether it could violate the propaganda law.
Democratic Sen. Jacky Rosen of Nevada has a bill to ban political ads featuring cabinet members that are paid for with tax dollars. She is trying to introduce an amendment to it Thursday to address at least the look and content of this new Trump spot.
Caitlin  Yilek , Gabe  Kaminsky and Arden  Farhi contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: France to Deploy Forces to Protect Saudi Red Sea Oil Port
articles.title_zh: France to Deploy Forces to Protect Saudi Red Sea Oil Port
articles.content_orig:
France is deploying military personnel and air defense equipment to protect Saudi Arabia's critical Red Sea oil terminal at Yanbu following recent drone and missile strikes. The terminal serves as a vital alternative export route bypassing the disrupted Strait of Hormuz, previously handling over 5 million barrels daily.
Market snapshot: French President Emmanuel Macron announced that France will deploy military assets, including troops, radar systems, and air defense systems, to safeguard Saudi Arabia's key Yanbu oil terminal. This strategic move aims to protect the terminal from Houthi rebel attacks without engaging France in active regional conflict. Before the recent strikes, the terminal and its connecting pipeline infrastructure handled crude exports exceeding 5 million barrels per day.
The deployment of French military resources to Yanbu is a clear signal that western nations view Saudi Arabia's Red Sea export infrastructure as a systemic global economic asset. With the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, any prolonged disruption at Yanbu would severely restrict global oil supply, prompting immediate defensive actions from major energy consumers like France.
The military shielding of Yanbu reduces the risk of long-term export blackouts, potentially capping immediate risk premiums in global crude pricing. However, the necessity of foreign military intervention highlights persistent geopolitical vulnerability, keeping oil prices highly sensitive to any further escalation.
While French military protection helps stabilize security around Yanbu, the ongoing Houthi threat and preceding pipeline disruptions keep global oil supplies tight. This balanced dynamic supports a neutral outlook for crude in the very near term as defensive measures are established.
Overweight: Oil & Gas Exploration, Energy Infrastructure Security
Underweight: Global Shipping & Logistics, Aviation
Time Horizon: Near-term (0-3 months)
Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline was designed to transport oil from eastern fields directly to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. With the Strait currently heavily restricted, Yanbu's role has expanded dramatically, transforming it from a secondary port into Saudi Arabia's primary energy pipeline outlet to global markets.
On September 10-11, 2026, drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West Crude Oil Pipeline forced a temporary shutdown, highlighting the vulnerability of the alternative Red Sea export route. On September 24, 2026, Saudi forces intercepted six ballistic missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu.
France's defensive deployment highlights the reality that securing alternative energy routes is now a national security priority for European powers. As long as maritime chokepoints remain contested, global energy security will increasingly rely on direct military underwriting.

articles.title_zh: US senators delay effort to permanently ban Chinese cars
articles.content_orig:
Proposed ban is a move to ensure that hundreds of thousands of US automotive jobs are not at risk of ‘total domination’ by Chinese car firms
The two US senators backing a permanent legislative ban on Chinese cars in the United States agreed on Thursday to delay their plan to use a fast track procedure to win Senate approval until next week, to seek the support of a lone holdout.
Republican Senator Bernie Moreno and Democratic Senator Elissa Slotkin had planned to seek ‌approval for the procedure – which requires unanimous Senate backing – on Thursday, the same day that US President Donald Trump met China’s President Xi Jinping in Washington.
But instead they will delay things and hold talks with Republican Senator Rand Paul, who had raised some concerns, in an effort to convince him to allow passage, congressional aides said.
Paul’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
